name: PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Molecular Diagnostic Criteria for PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum

criteria.description: Presence of somatic activating mutation in PIK3CA gene confirmed by molecular testing
Asymmetric segmental overgrowth of soft tissue, bone, or both
Presence of vascular anomalies such as capillary, venous, or lymphatic malformations
Exclusion of other genetic overgrowth syndromes by clinical and molecular evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of somatic activating PIK3CA mutation plus clinical evidence of segmental overgrowth
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular confirmation is critical due to phenotypic overlap with other overgrowth syndromes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Asymmetric segmental soft tissue and bony overgrowth

pathognomonic.notes: May cause localized swelling and cystic lesions

common.notes: Due to overgrowth and vascular anomalies

occasional.notes: Due to nerve compression by overgrowth
Spinal curvature related to asymmetric growth
Due to lymphatic or venous obstruction

rare.notes: Involvement of liver, spleen, or kidneys
Associated with brain involvement in rare cases
Rarely reported, possibly secondary to chronic disease burden

laboratory: Molecular genetic testing identifying somatic PIK3CA activating mutations in affected tissue
imaging: MRI showing asymmetric soft tissue and bone overgrowth
CT or MRI angiography for detailed vascular mapping
genetic: Somatic activating mutations in PIK3CA gene (e.g., H1047R, E545K)
other: Histopathology of affected tissue showing vascular malformations and cellular overgrowth

distinguishingFeatures: Triad of capillary malformation, venous malformation, and limb hypertrophy
No confirmed PIK3CA mutation in all cases
Usually involves entire limb rather than segmental overgrowth

redFlags: Rapid progression of overgrowth causing functional impairment
Signs of visceral organ involvement or neurological symptoms
references: Keppler-Noreuil KM et al. PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum (PROS): Diagnostic and Testing Eligibility Criteria, Differential Diagnosis, and Evaluation. Am J Med Genet A. 2015.
Lindhurst MJ et al. A mosaic activating mutation in AKT1 associated with the Proteus syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2011.
Mirzaa GM et al. PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum (PROS): Clinical and Molecular Characteristics. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2016.
